newsitem.title: USA: NY agencies unveil proposals for NYC Coliseum site.
newsitem.headline: NY agencies unveil proposals for NYC Coliseum site.

text.p: The Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which owns the New York Coliseum in New York City, on Monday, said it unveiled nine plans for buying and developing the 3.43-acre site, located at Colombus Circle.

The agency, which was joined by the Empire State Development Corp, plans to hold a public hearing on January 23 to address the environmental impact of a new building, which would be limited to a height of 750 feet and no more than 2.1 million square feet.

A spokesman for the Empire State Development Corp declined to disclose how much the nine developers are prepared to pay for the site. "No one here will characterize any dollar figures at all, period," said John Melia.

The New York Post, in its Monday edition, said that Millenium Partners has offered about $225 million, adding Donald Trump has told his partners that their $300 million offer is the highest. The newspaper said that at least one other bidder is ready to pay up to $250 million.
The spokesman for the Empire State Development Agency added that it expects to release a short list of bidders this winter, and announce the winner this spring.

"What we're trying to do is ensure all the stakeholders are represented and have the information they need, and to have hard and fast deadlines is counterproductive," Melia said, explaining that stakeholders was a term used to describe community groups, elected officials and other interested parties. The Post had said the short list would be released on February 1 and the winning bid disclosed on March 15.
Melia added the agency was taking a more flexible approach to try to avoid the stiff opposition that blocked its previous attempt to develop the site.
